title: Adapter and Bridge
idea: Adapter wraps a class with the wrong interface to fit the one your code expects. Bridge splits a class into two hierarchies, linked by has-a, that vary independently.
points: An adapter implements your interface and translates each call for the wrapped object.
Adapter fixes a mismatch after the fact, often around code you cannot edit.
Bridge is planned up front: the abstraction holds an implementor in a field.
With Bridge, three alerts and three channels need six classes, not nine.

hero.title: Wrap to fit; split to grow

steps.caption: Adapter: checkout code calls `pay` on the `PaymentGateway` interface it owns.
`BankAdapter` implements that interface, so checkout never sees the vendor class.
It renames the call, turns pounds into pence and maps the status code back.
Bridge: one hierarchy says what an alert is. `Notice` and `Urgent` extend `Alert`.
`Alert` holds a `Channel` in a field. That has-a link is the bridge.
Channels grow on their own side. A new channel works with every alert at once.

code.title: Adapter
code.caption: Checkout speaks `PaymentGateway`. The adapter turns that into the vendor's calls and codes. Real money uses `BigDecimal` or minor units; `double` keeps it short.

walk.text: The target: the interface your code is written against.
The adaptee: other method names, amounts in pence, numeric result codes.
The adapter wraps the vendor object it receives through its constructor.
It converts units and renames the call.
It maps the vendor's status code to your own `PAID` or `DECLINED` result.
`main` sees only `PaymentGateway`; swapping vendors means a new adapter.

code.title: Bridge
code.caption: Two alert kinds times two channels, with no `UrgentSmsAlert` class anywhere.

walk.text: The implementor interface: how a message physically goes out.
Two concrete channels. They know nothing about alert kinds.
The abstraction keeps a `Channel` in a `final` field: the bridge.
Refined alerts decide the wording, then delegate delivery to the channel.
Any alert pairs with any channel at run time.

pitfalls: Keep adapters thin: translate calls and data, and put business rules elsewhere.
Map vendor errors to your own results or exceptions; never leak vendor codes upward.
Skip Bridge when only one dimension varies; plain composition or Strategy is enough.

quiz.q: What is the first line `AdapterDemo` prints?
quiz.why: The vendor prints before `pay` returns. `Math.round` on a `double` returns a `long`, so 12.5 becomes 1250 with no decimal point.

takeaway: Adapter makes an existing class fit; Bridge keeps two dimensions apart.
